propositions: A configured provider is silently discarded when the model id contains a colon in the version suffix (canonical Bedrock form), causing the string to be returned unqualified and the explicit provider setting to be ignored.

The qualifier detection logic incorrectly treats any colon in a model string as a provider separator, failing to distinguish between a separator colon and a colon in the version suffix of Bedrock model ids.

The two independent implementations of the qualified/unqualified test (_resolve_target and infer_provider) can drift apart and both fail in the same way, implementing the same faulty logic separately.

When resolution fails due to the dropped provider, the error message misleadingly names a fragment of the model id as the unknown provider, contradicting the operator's explicit configuration and obscuring the actual cause.
An explicitly configured provider must be checked before scanning the model string, so that no punctuation in the model id can overrule or discard an explicit instruction.
